results.title: Jakarta overtakes Tokyo as world’s most populous city, according to UN | Indonesia | The Guardian
results.label: yes
results.reason: report_index/international_other: UN World Urbanisation Prospects 2025 report data on global megacities.

notes.subject: society
notes.why_in_news: The UN World Urbanisation Prospects 2025 report identifies Jakarta as the world's most populous city due to revised geospatial and population criteria.
notes.fact_box: Jakarta's population is estimated at 42 million, surpassing Tokyo (33 million) and Dhaka (37 million). The UN report notes that urban dwellers now comprise nearly half of the world's 8.2 billion people.

prelims_pointers.text: Jakarta population: 42 million (UN World Urbanisation Prospects 2025)
Tokyo population: 33 million (defined as a megalopolis including Saitama, Chiba, and Kanagawa)
Number of megacities (10M+ inhabitants) increased from 8 in 1975 to 33 in 2025
Global urban population growth: 20% in 1950 to nearly 50% currently
Projected urban growth: Two-thirds of global population growth expected in cities by 2050

notes.mains_question: Discuss the socio-economic implications of rapid urbanisation in Asian megacities and the challenges of managing inclusive urban growth by 2050.
mains_dimensions: Infrastructure strain: Rapid expansion of megacities like Jakarta and Dhaka outstripping municipal waste and transit capacities
Spatial delimitation: Challenges in standardizing urban boundaries for accurate policy planning and resource allocation
Climate vulnerability: High population density in coastal megacities increasing exposure to sea-level rise and extreme weather

results.title: India-UAE FTA Talks: Market access, gold quota and data sharing reviewed under CEPA - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: economy/international_india: Trade data, FTA review, and gold quota targets are key economic facts.

notes.subject: ir
notes.why_in_news: India and the UAE held a joint committee meeting to review the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to enhance trade and regulatory cooperation.
notes.fact_box: Bilateral trade between India and UAE exceeded $100 billion in 2024-25, marking a 19.6% growth over 2023-24. The nations have set a target to reach $100 billion in non-oil and non-precious metal trade by 2030.

prelims_pointers.text: CEPA: A Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the UAE.
Bilateral trade volume: Crossed $100 billion in the 2024-25 period.
Target: $100 billion in non-oil and non-precious metal trade by 2030.
APEDA: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, involved in food safety MoUs.
Gold TRQ: India now allocates gold Tariff Rate Quotas through a transparent competitive bidding process.

notes.mains_question: Examine how Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) can serve as catalysts for diversifying India's export basket beyond traditional commodities.
mains_dimensions: Trade diversification: Shifting focus from oil/precious metals to high-value non-oil and non-precious metal exports by 2030.
Regulatory alignment: Harmonizing food safety standards and pharmaceutical regulations to reduce non-tariff barriers.
Transparency in quotas: Utilizing competitive bidding for Gold Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQ) to ensure market integrity.

results.title: Proposal for new design of border fencing under consideration of Centre: BSF IG - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: internal_security/national: Border management and infrastructure updates on India-Bangladesh border.

notes.subject: security
notes.why_in_news: The BSF IG announced that the Ministry of Home Affairs is considering a proposal for a new design of barbed wire fencing along the India-Bangladesh border to replace aging infrastructure.
notes.fact_box: India shares a 4,096 km international border with Bangladesh, with Tripura accounting for 856 km of this stretch. The BSF is currently working with the Bangladesh Border Guard (BGB) on joint patrolling and cattle smuggling prevention.

prelims_pointers.text: India-Bangladesh international border length is 4,096 km.
Tripura shares 856 km of its border with Bangladesh.
BSF (Border Security Force) operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
BGB (Border Guard Bangladesh) is the primary border guarding agency of Bangladesh.

notes.mains_question: Discuss the significance of integrated border management and infrastructure modernization in curbing transnational crimes like cattle smuggling along the India-Bangladesh border.
mains_dimensions: Infrastructure degradation: Accelerated decay of existing barbed wire fencing due to heavy rainfall and extreme weather in the Northeast.
Operational synergy: Importance of 'Joint Patrolling' and 'Casualty Contact' protocols between BSF and BGB to maintain regional stability.
Transnational crime mitigation: Challenges in policing 'border haats' and zero-line areas to prevent organized cattle smuggling.
